ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE ACCEPTABLE USE POLICY

Halbrook Diagnostics, Inc.
Adopted by the Board of Directors on March 3, 2026
Owner: Chief Information Security Officer
Review cycle: annually, and upon any material change in law or in the tools approved under this policy

1. PURPOSE

This policy states how a director, officer, employee, or contractor of Halbrook Diagnostics, Inc. may use artificial intelligence and generative AI tools in the course of company work, what use is prohibited, and what review a person must apply before relying on an AI output. It is written to the NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0) and, for the company's activity in the European Union, to the EU AI Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/1689.

2. SCOPE

This policy applies to every person who performs work for the company, on any device, whether the tool is licensed by the company, embedded in another product the company uses, or reached through a free public website. It applies to every AI system as that term is defined in Article 3(1) of the EU AI Act, and to every generative AI tool that produces text, code, images, audio, or video.

3. APPROVED AI TOOLS

Only a tool listed on the AI Tool Register maintained by the Chief Information Security Officer may be used for company work. A tool is added to the register only after security review, data-protection review, and a written record of the vendor's training-data and retention terms. A person who wants a tool added submits a request through the IT service desk. Use of a tool that is not on the register is a violation of this policy, and no exception is effective unless it is granted in writing by the Chief Information Security Officer.

4. PROHIBITED INPUTS

A person may not enter any of the following into an AI tool, whether approved or not:

(a) protected health information, as defined at 45 C.F.R. § 160.103;
(b) personal data of any identified or identifiable natural person, other than the person's own business contact information;
(c) a trade secret of the company or of any third party;
(d) information subject to the attorney-client privilege or prepared in anticipation of litigation;
(e) unpublished financial results, or any other material nonpublic information;
(f) source code of the company's regulated device software; and
(g) any information a customer, partner, or regulator has given the company under an obligation of confidentiality, unless the applicable agreement permits the disclosure.

5. PROHIBITED USES

A person may not use an AI tool to make or to materially influence a decision about a person's employment, promotion, compensation, or termination; about a patient's diagnosis, treatment, or eligibility for care; about the extension or denial of credit; or about any other matter that Annex III of the EU AI Act treats as high risk, except under a written protocol approved by the AI Governance Committee that provides for human oversight under Article 14 of that Regulation.

A person may not use an AI tool to generate content that impersonates a real person, to produce a synthetic image or recording of a real person without that person's written consent, or to circumvent a technical protection measure.

6. HUMAN REVIEW

An AI output is a draft, never a work product. A person who uses an AI output in company work is responsible for it as if the person had written it, and must review it for accuracy, for legal sufficiency, and for hallucination before it is relied upon, sent outside the company, filed with a regulator, or committed to a code repository. A citation, a statute, a study, or a quotation that an AI tool produces must be verified against the underlying source before it is used. No AI output may be filed with the Food and Drug Administration or with any court without review and sign-off by the responsible officer.

7. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY AND ATTRIBUTION

Under the guidance published by the United States Patent and Trademark Office, a natural person must have made a significant contribution to any claimed invention; an AI tool is not an inventor. A person who uses an AI tool in the conception of an invention must record the person's own contribution in the invention disclosure. Under the practices of the United States Copyright Office, material generated by an AI tool without sufficient human authorship is not protected by copyright, and the company does not claim copyright in such material.

A person may not represent AI-generated material as the person's own original work where the recipient's decision depends on its authorship, including in a regulatory submission, a scientific publication, or a response to a customer audit.

8. DISCLOSURE

Where the company makes an AI system available to a natural person, the company discloses that the person is interacting with an AI system, as Article 50 of the EU AI Act requires. Synthetic content the company publishes is marked as machine-generated.

9. TRAINING

Each person who performs work for the company completes AI use training upon hire or engagement and annually thereafter. The Chief Information Security Officer maintains a record of completion for seven years.

10. INCIDENT REPORTING

A person who becomes aware of a prohibited input, a materially inaccurate AI output that has left the company, an AI tool that has behaved in an unexpected or unsafe way, or a suspected breach of an AI vendor must report it to the Chief Information Security Officer within twenty-four hours. The company investigates each report, records the outcome, and reports to the AI Governance Committee quarterly.

11. GOVERNANCE

The AI Governance Committee is chaired by the Chief Information Security Officer and includes the General Counsel, the Chief Medical Officer, and the head of Quality. The Committee maintains the AI Tool Register, approves each high-risk protocol, reviews this policy annually, and reports to the Audit Committee of the Board at least twice each year.

12. CONSEQUENCES

A violation of this policy may result in discipline up to and including termination of employment or of the engagement, and may be reported to a regulator or to law enforcement where the law requires.

13. QUESTIONS

A question about this policy is directed to the Chief Information Security Officer at aigovernance@halbrookdx.example.
